scope: frontend code only — demo-app/web/src/lib/apiClient.ts, demo-app/web/src/lib/session.ts, demo-app/web/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx, demo-app/web/src/pages/Login.tsx

evidence.observation: Access token is stored in a module-level variable that is never persisted to localStorage, sessionStorage, or cookies. It initializes to null on every page load.
After successful login, the access token is set in memory, then the page is redirected to '/'. Token exists only in memory.
Dashboard makes three concurrent API calls on mount without any error handling. If any fail with 401, multiple refresh attempts will be triggered simultaneously.
api() function handles 401 by calling refreshSession(), but has no mutex/lock to prevent multiple simultaneous refresh attempts. Each 401 response independently triggers a refresh.
refreshSession() updates _accessToken module variable synchronously after fetch completes, but there is no coordination between concurrent refresh calls.
logout() sets _accessToken to null and navigates to /login, but does NOT wait for the logout request to complete. window.location.href assignment happens immediately.
When refresh fails, logout() is called which immediately redirects to /login. Any other in-flight requests still waiting will not have their completion awaited.
After refresh, the original request is retried. If refresh failed but returned true (race condition), newToken could be null or stale, causing the retry to also fail.

hypotheses.statement: Access token is lost on page reload because it is stored only in memory (module variable _accessToken), not persisted to localStorage/sessionStorage. When user refreshes, _accessToken resets to null, causing all API requests to fail with 401 and immediately log them out.

When Dashboard mounts on page reload with no token in memory, three concurrent api() calls (F3) all receive 401 responses. Each independently calls refreshSession() without mutex synchronization, creating a race condition where multiple refresh requests are sent and one may succeed while others fail or receive conflicting responses.

When a refresh attempt fails, one concurrent request calls logout() (F6) which immediately navigates to /login (F7) without awaiting the logout fetch. Other in-flight api() calls are interrupted mid-execution, leaving the user in an inconsistent state without error visibility.

The retry after refresh (F8) may receive a null or stale token if multiple refreshSession() calls race each other. If one refresh succeeds but updates _accessToken after another has already read it as null, the retry will fail with the same 401, causing immediate logout.
